title: NAFv4.1 · UAF-based structural application profile
description: All 47 NAFv4.1 (2026.03) viewpoint IDs with executable structural checks, inherited UAF 1.0 types and explicit application adapters. Use @help viewpoints naf41-uaf ID and @help connections naf41-uaf TYPE.
sources: ReferenceDocs/nafv4/NAFv4-ADMBw-MDG-2026.05.xml — supporting comparison only; its declared foundation is NAF 4.0
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
No certification or complete NAF/UAF conformance is claimed. All 47 IDs are covered structurally, not all normative semantics.
The inherited UAF coverage report still applies, including deferred native constraints. Application adapters are identified in type help.
Only included view elements/links count toward viewpoint connection rules. Typed references resolve in the model; designated structural references must also be visible.
NAF methodology, stakeholder approval, full state/sequence execution semantics and qualitative completeness require human review. See profiles/naf41/COVERAGE.md.

Service.description: NAF S1 vocabulary resolved to UAF 1.0 ServiceSpecification in this application profile. ActualService remains distinct.
limitations: UAF 1.2 renamed ServiceSpecification to Service alongside other service metamodel changes. This alias retains UAF 1.0 semantics; it does not claim cross-version equivalence.

Node.description: NAF S2/L1 Node vocabulary for the existing logical-node application type. Its UAF projection is OperationalArchitecture through LogicalNode, not OperationalPerformer or a physical System.
limitations: Explicit arch.js application mapping. This is not a native UAF or ADMBw stereotype named Node, nor an assertion that every OperationalArchitecture must be called Node.

ServiceOperation.description: NAF S3 operation vocabulary resolved to UAF 1.0 ServiceMethod, which extends UML Operation. This alias retains the native runtime rules and written source name.
limitations: Application vocabulary mapping, not a claim that all native UML operation-owner, method and ownedParameter constraints are implemented.

mappings.description: Explicit application-profile vocabulary equivalence for S1. Executable identity is defined separately by aliases.nodeTypes.Service.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

mappings.description: Documented UAF rename. Descriptive only: other service concepts and relationships also changed in UAF 1.2.
limitations: No automatic UAF 1.0 to 1.2 model conversion or complete semantic equivalence is asserted.

mappings.description: Application projection of NAF logical grouping nodes through LogicalNode extends OperationalArchitecture. Node is a vocabulary alias of LogicalNode within arch.js, not an alias of the entire UAF OperationalArchitecture category.

mappings.description: Concrete application subtype for the NAF example vocabulary. ResourcePerformer remains abstract and retains its native attributes; this is deliberately not an alias.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

mappings.description: Application-profile operation vocabulary equivalence. Native ServiceMethod extends UML Operation; deferred native ownership/method constraints remain outside the structural projection.

DesiresVision.description: Enterprise phase to desired vision, as shown in the C2 cut-out and the p.91 example.

DesiresGoal.description: Enterprise phase to desired goal, as shown in the C2 cut-out.

CharacterizesCapability.description: Performance criterion to the capability characterized, following the C7 cut-out direction.

CharacterizesEffect.description: Effectiveness criterion to the effect assessed.

ConstrainsCapability.description: Planning constraint to the capability constrained.

OriginatesFromRationale.description: Constraint to its originating rationale, following the C8 cut-out. JustifiesStrategy remains the explicit inverse application relationship.

RelatesToEnterprisePhase.description: Capability increment to a related planning enterprise phase, following the Cr cut-out and p.103 example. Distinct from AchievedEffect, whose target must be an ActualState.

AggregatesEnterprisePhase.description: Whole planning phase to a temporal subphase, following aggregates on pp.102–103. Binary application projection of temporal membership, not an imported UAF TemporalPart property or UML composition.

TriggersEnterprisePhase.description: Triggering planning phase to a following phase, following triggers on pp.102–103. A directed planning dependency, not an executable state transition or a calculated date constraint.

ServiceAggregation.description: Whole service to a member service, following aggregates in the S2 cut-out and p.108 example. A separate directed grouping relation, not an alias of ServiceComposition and not exclusive composition ownership.
limitations: Binary application projection rendered as a solid directed link. Self-links/cycles are disallowed; multiple aggregating services may reference the same member. Full UML shared-aggregation, ownership and lifecycle semantics are not implemented.

ServiceDependency.description: Dependent service to required service. Restricted service-to-service subset of the ADMBw relationship.

ConsumesService.description: Logical node or explicit S4 consumer role to the service it consumes. Native UAF Consumes remains OperationalActivity to ServiceSpecification.

EnablesService.description: Service function to the service it enables, following the S2 cut-out and p.108 example. The native IsCapableToPerform relation remains service to function.

RealizesService.description: Physical active resource to the service it realizes, following the S2 cut-out and p.108 example. Native Implements retains its UAF endpoint pairs.

ServiceFunctionAggregation.description: Whole function to constituent function. Shared membership is permitted; not UML exclusive ownership or executable activity decomposition.

ProvidesService.description: Provider role to the service it provides.

NotifiesServiceProvider.description: Service function to the provider role it notifies.

AccessesServiceFunction.description: Consumer role to the function it accesses.

SupportsServiceFunction.description: Operational activity to the function it supports. Distinct from the inverse enables projection.

EnablesOperationalActivity.description: Service function to the operational activity it enables.

PerformsOperationalActivity.description: Provider or consumer role to an operational activity it performs. Native IsCapableToPerform is retained independently.

AggregatesServiceGroup.description: Whole service group to a member group, following the recursive grouping in the S1 cut-out. Acyclic binary membership projection, not strong UML composition.

HasServiceOperationParameter.description: Service operation to its conceptual parameter, following has on pp.109–110. The same parameter may be associated with multiple operations; this is not UML exclusive ownership.

InvolvesPhysicalResource.description: Service operation parameter to the physical passive resource or data product it involves, following pp.109–110. Data Model trace is indirect through that resource; DataModel is not a valid direct target.

ServicePolicySatisfiedBy.description: Policy to a service satisfying it. Retained inverse application relationship; use SatisfiesServicePolicy for the service-to-policy direction shown on pp.104–105.

SatisfiesServicePolicy.description: Service to the policy it satisfies, following the S1 cut-out and p.105 example. ServicePolicySatisfiedBy remains the explicit inverse application relationship.

GroupsLogicalResource.description: Logical node to the resources/behavior it groups.

LogicalDependency.description: Logical structural dependency. A Needline is modeled separately.

LogicalInteraction.description: Binary projection of a logical interaction with explicit payload; use needline to reference its need. The default connected presentation uses reference cards attached to the flow, following the example on page 132 with the original arch.js templates and colors.

LogicalControlFlow.description: Control flow between activity definitions (adapter, not UML action-level OperationalControlFlow).

LogicalObjectFlow.description: Flow of logical passive resources between activity definitions.

TracesStrategicConstraint.description: Logical constraint to strategic constraint traced.

FulfilsLogicalReadiness.description: Logical active resource to readiness level fulfilled.

TracesCapabilityIncrement.description: Logical readiness to capability increment traced.

GroupsPhysicalResource.description: Capability configuration to member active/passive resource.

PhysicalDependency.description: Physical active resource to required active/passive resource.

InteractionConformsTo.description: Interaction to governing standard/protocol. Protocol is a UAF Standard subtype.

ResourceImplementsProtocol.description: Resource to implemented protocol; direct projection, not ADMBw ProtocolImplementation reification.

FunctionalFlow.description: Control flow between function definitions (not action-level FunctionControlFlow).

TracesInformationModel.description: Data model to information model traced.

TracesLogicalConstraint.description: Resource constraint to logical constraint traced.

DeliversResourceReadiness.description: Configuration to delivered resource readiness level.

TracesLogicalReadiness.description: Resource readiness to logical readiness traced.

DefinesGlossaryTerm.description: Architecture description to relevant glossary term.

ContainsView.description: Architecture description to constituent view. Same direction as ADMBw ViewsInArchitecturalDescription.

ConformsToViewpoint.description: View to governing viewpoint (also retain the native viewpoint reference).

StakeholderHasConcern.description: Stakeholder to concern. Same direction as ADMBw StakeholderConcern.

FramesConcern.description: Viewpoint to framed concern. Same direction as ADMBw ConcernForViewpoint.

C1.title: Capability Taxonomy
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

C2.title: Enterprise Vision
C2.description: Vision, goals, enterprise phases and capabilities linked to them.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
EnterprisePhase is the required planning-phase representation in this mapping; ActualEnterprisePhase can additionally record actual states.

The C2 cut-out permits desires from an enterprise phase to a capability, vision or goal. Every planning phase requires at least one of these links; a direct DesiresCapability is not mandatory when DesiresVision/DesiresGoal is present.

C3.title: Capability Dependencies
C3.description: Dependencies between capabilities, with optional specialization and grouping context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Not every displayed capability must have a CapabilityDependency: specialization/grouping context is allowed, as SAR demonstrates in the p.93 example. The view requires at least one dependency; completeness of relevant real-world dependencies cannot be checked automatically.

C4.title: Standard Processes
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

C5.title: Effects
C5.description: Effects desired by capabilities and optional effectiveness criteria.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

C7.title: Performance Criteria
C7.description: Capabilities characterized by assessment criteria evaluated by measures, with optional effectiveness criteria.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

EffectivenessCriterion and its subtypes are excluded from the per-assessment-criterion mandatory characterization/evaluation checks. Their links are optional, following p.98 and the Time to find example on p.99. Ordinary assessment criteria still require the complete capability-criterion-measure chain.

EvaluatesCriterion is directed from Measure to AssessmentCriterion, following the p.98 cut-out. The evaluates arrows on p.99 are drawn in the opposite direction; that illustration does not change endpoint compatibility.

C8.title: Planning Constraints
C8.description: Strategic constraints applied to capabilities. Constraint extends StrategicConstraint and supports the p.101 example vocabulary.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Cr.title: Capability Roadmap
Cr.description: Increments deliver capabilities and may relate to planning phases with temporal grouping and trigger dependencies. Supports the p.103 presentation with implicit milestone properties.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

The p.103 example omits explicit milestone nodes because milestones are properties of an increment. Cr therefore does not require visible CapabilityMilestone nodes or incoming DefinesIncrement at every increment. Explicit visible milestones still require a DefinesIncrement link; the optional milestones reference attribute may point to model elements outside the view. Implicit milestone completeness is not checked.

AggregatesEnterprisePhase and TriggersEnterprisePhase are authored binary application adapters, directed whole-to-part and triggering-to-following phase. Each type is acyclic and disallows self-links as an application rule. No single-parent ownership, UML TemporalPart/slot semantics, execution, guards or date ordering between phases is inferred.

CapabilityIncrement is a distinct UAFElement adapter, not an ActualEnterprisePhase/Achiever/ActualState. Earlier implicit compatibility with AchievedEffect and ActualEnterprisePhase relationships no longer applies. Optional startDate/endDate retain ISO date-time validation and ordering.
Connected views reproduce the explanatory p.103 structure. A time-based Gantt representation needs actual schedule dates; the sample does not invent them.

S1.title: Service Taxonomy
S1.description: Service specialization taxonomy. Service is a vocabulary alias of UAF 1.0 ServiceSpecification in this application profile; policies and nested groups are optional context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Service aliases ServiceSpecification in both directions, preserving written labels and inherited service rules. This is not an implementation of the UAF 1.2 service metamodel. ServiceGeneralization points from the specialized service to its general service. Multiple inheritance is permitted by the profile; a whole-view tree still requires one hierarchy parent per node.

SatisfiesServicePolicy points from service to policy, following pp.104–105. ServicePolicySatisfiedBy is the retained inverse application link, not a direction change to existing models. Native ServicePolicy still requires its ruleKind attribute; the p.105 drawing does not specify that value.

GroupsService connects a ServiceGroup to a member service; AggregatesServiceGroup connects a group to a member group. The latter disallows self-links/cycles as an application rule, without imposing single-parent ownership or strong composition.
Use a Connected view with a ServiceGeneralization-only tree group when policy/group context is present. A whole-view tree may filter to ServiceGeneralization, omitting non-hierarchy edges.

S2.title: Service Structure
S2.description: Service aggregation, composition and dependencies; optional interfaces, functions, logical nodes and physical realizations.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Node is an alias of the application LogicalNode, a subtype of OperationalArchitecture. This models the logical grouping/architecture meaning of a NAF Node, not a physical System, runtime instance or drawing template.

The pp.107–108 directions are node to service (ConsumesService), function to service (EnablesService), and physical active resource to service (RealizesService). Native Consumes, IsCapableToPerform and Implements are unchanged; they are not interchangeable aliases of these adapters.

ServiceAggregation projects whole service to member service (aggregates in the source), with a solid directed link and no exclusive ownership. ServiceComposition remains a separate relationship with composition notation. Both reject cycles/self-links; full UML ownership/lifecycle semantics are not implemented. ServiceDependency remains dependent service to required service.

Per-service structural checks count ServiceAggregation/ServiceComposition/ServiceDependency, not optional node/function/resource traces. Service Consumer and Service Provider role projections and their relies-on/provides/delivers relationships are not yet implemented as dedicated NAF concepts; do not substitute generic nodes or native Consumes for those roles.

S3.title: Service Interfaces
S3.description: Services specify interfaces and optional operations with shared conceptual parameters and optional physical data-product traces.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

ServiceOperation is an application-profile vocabulary alias of UAF ServiceMethod (a UML Operation stereotype). DataProductType is a separate DataElement/PhysicalPassiveResource specialization. Native UAF and ADMBw definitions are unchanged.

HasServiceOperationParameter runs from operation to parameter; InvolvesPhysicalResource runs from parameter to a physical passive resource/data product. The p.110 Geographic Location parameter is shared by two operations. These are conceptual associations, not exclusive UML Parameter ownership.

Legacy owner/resource references remain valid and, when provided, must be visible. An owner reference can satisfy the required operation association instead of a has link; identical link/reference evidence is counted once. S3 does not require a resource for every parameter, matching the Resource parameter in p.110.

An optional DataModel trace uses SpecifiesData from model to DataElement/DataProductType. A parameter does not link directly to a DataModel. Full UML operation signatures, parameter ordering/directions and consistency between simultaneous link/reference declarations require review.

S4.title: Service Functions
S4.description: Functions enabling services, recursive function aggregation, provider/consumer roles and operational activity context.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Each selected function must enable a selected service directly or through selected aggregating ancestors. Legacy service-to-function IsCapableToPerform remains accepted. This is contextual coverage, not inheritance of behavior or implicit model edges.

Provider and consumer are explicit contextual application roles, with optional represents references. Cut-out links are directed structural projections; no execution, notification delivery, exclusive ownership or full UML activity decomposition is asserted.

S5.title: Service States
S5.description: Service states, transitions, events and function modes.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
Transition guards, state ownership consistency, reachability and execution are not evaluated.

S6.title: Service Sequence
S6.description: Ordered interactions between lifelines representing services.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
Order is a positive integer; UML interaction fragments, time semantics and unique sequence positions require review.

S7.title: Service Interface Parameters
S7.description: Operation/function parameters reference their owner and passive resource.
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.

Use ServiceOperationParameter or ServiceFunctionParameter: the unqualified UAF ServiceParameter lacks the required owner/payload projection. Operation parameters may use explicit has/involves links instead of owner/resource references; S7 requires both associations, whereas S3 makes the resource trace optional.

S8.title: Service Constraints
limitations: Structural application mapping in arch.js; not the complete UML/SysML semantics or an official NATO/OMG implementation guide.
